title: Rise in ADHD Cases Raises Questions
credits: Mike Stobbe reported this story for the Associated Press from New York, New York. Anna Matteo adapted it for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: Allison Burk’s daughter was struggling.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森·伯克的女儿正在挣扎。

sentences.en: The American teenager had uncontrolled emotions, a decreased ability to pay attention and trouble completing work on time.
sentences.zh: 这个美国青少年情绪失控，注意力难以集中，而且难以按时完成作业。

sentences.en: A family doctor suggested testing for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, or ADHD.
sentences.zh: 一位家庭医生建议使用药物测试注意力缺陷/多动症，或ADHD。

sentences.en: This led to an unexpected discovery: The teen had ADHD, and her mother, Allison Burk, did too.
sentences.zh: 这导致了一个意想不到的发现：这个青少年患有ADHD，她的母亲艾莉森·伯克也患有ADHD。

sentences.en: During her daughter’s testing, Burk thought, “Wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 在女儿进行测试期间，伯克心想，'等一下。

sentences.en: This sounds familiar.”
sentences.zh: 这听起来很熟悉。'

sentences.en: “I was able to piece together that this might be something I was experiencing,” said Burk, who lives in Columbus, Ohio.
sentences.zh: 伯克说：'我能够拼凑出这可能是我正在经历的事情。'，她住在俄亥俄州的哥伦布市。

sentences.en: She sought testing for herself and was diagnosed with ADHD — at 42 years old.
sentences.zh: 她为自己寻求测试，并在42岁时被诊断出患有ADHD。

sentences.en: More adults are being diagnosed with ADHD.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的成年人被诊断出患有ADHD。

sentences.en: Diagnoses have been rising for at least 20 years but seem to have increased sharply in the last few years.
sentences.zh: 诊断数量至少已经上升了20年，但似乎在最近几年急剧增加。

sentences.en: A recent government study suggested that more than 15 million adults in the United States — about 1 in 17 — have been diagnosed with ADHD.
sentences.zh: 最近的一项政府研究表明，美国有超过1500万成年人——大约每17人中就有1人——被诊断出患有ADHD。

sentences.en: The condition starts in childhood, but about half of adults with ADHD are diagnosed when they are 18 or older.
sentences.zh: 这种情况始于童年，但约有一半的ADHD成年人在18岁或更大年龄时被诊断出来。

sentences.en: Some doctors say the number of people seeking ADHD testing is sharply increasing.
sentences.zh: 一些医生说，寻求ADHD测试的人数正在急剧增加。

sentences.en: “Just in our clinic, requests for assessments have doubled in the last two years,” said Justin Barterian.
sentences.zh: '仅仅在我们的诊所，过去两年里对评估的请求就翻了一番，'贾斯汀·巴特利安说。

sentences.en: He is a psychologist based at Ohio State University.
sentences.zh: 他是一位基于俄亥俄州立大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: ADHD makes it hard for people to pay attention and control their behaviors.
sentences.zh: ADHD使人们难以集中注意力和控制自己的行为。

sentences.en: The disorder can be genetic.
sentences.zh: 这种疾病可能是遗传的。

sentences.en: Doctors often treat the disorder with drugs, behavioral therapy, or both.
sentences.zh: 医生通常用药物治疗、行为疗法，或两者结合来治疗这种疾病。

sentences.en: Judy Sandler is 62 years old and lives in the U.S. state of Maine.
sentences.zh: 朱迪·桑德兰62岁，生活在美国缅因州。

sentences.en: She was diagnosed in her 50s.
sentences.zh: 她在50多岁时被诊断出来。

sentences.en: Sandler describes what ADHD feels like for her.
sentences.zh: 桑德勒描述了多动症对她而言是什么感受。

sentences.en: “It’s like there’s an engine in you and you feel like it’s always running, and you can’t turn it off except with medication,” Sandler said.
sentences.zh: 桑德勒说：'就像你体内有一台引擎，你感觉它一直在运转，除了靠药物，你无法让它停下来。'

sentences.en: ADHD has been called the most commonly diagnosed mental health disorder in American children.
sentences.zh: 多动症被称为美国儿童中最常见的精神健康疾病。

sentences.en: More than 7 million children in the U.S. have been diagnosed.
sentences.zh: 美国已有超过700万名儿童被确诊。

sentences.en: The disorder was once thought to be something that resolved as children became adults.
sentences.zh: 这种疾病曾被认为是随着儿童成长为成人而会消失的问题。

sentences.en: But now, experts say they believe that many people are not diagnosed as kids and that the disorder continues into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 但现在，专家表示，他们认为许多人小时候并未被确诊，且这种疾病会持续到成年。

sentences.en: Adults with the condition talk about having trouble focusing on immediate responsibilities and planning their time.
sentences.zh: 患有此病的成年人表示，他们在专注于眼前的责任和规划时间方面存在困难。

sentences.en: Some say the disorder has led to problems in their personal relationships.
sentences.zh: 有人说这种疾病给他们的个人关系带来了问题。

sentences.en: Diagnoses have been rising
sentences.zh: 确诊数量一直在上升

sentences.en: Diagnoses have been increasing in both kids and adults.
sentences.zh: 儿童和成年人的确诊数量都在增加。

sentences.en: The recent government report also found adult ADHD was more common than earlier estimates had suggested.
sentences.zh: 最近的一份政府报告还发现，成人的多动症比早期估计所提示的更为普遍。

sentences.en: “We haven’t had (federal) adult ADHD data in a long time,” said Angelika Claussen.
sentences.zh: 桑德勒说：'我们已经很久没有（联邦层面）成人多动症的数据了。'

sentences.en: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention researcher was one of the study’s writers.
sentences.zh: 这位美国疾病控制与预防中心的研究人员是这项研究的作者之一。

sentences.en: There were signs of the rise, she added.
sentences.zh: 她还补充说，已经出现了上升的迹象。

sentences.en: Increasing demand for ADHD medication led to severe shortages after the COVID-19 pandemic hit in March 2020.
sentences.zh: 对多动症药物需求的增加，在2020年3月新冠疫情爆发后导致了严重的短缺。

sentences.en: A 2023 study showed the rise in prescriptions, or doctors’ orders for such medication, was notable in adults — especially among women.
sentences.zh: 一项2023年的研究表明，处方量的上升，即医生对这类药物的开具，在成年人中尤为显著——尤其是女性。

sentences.en: ADHD diagnoses and medication were increasing before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 在新冠疫情爆发之前，多动症的确诊和用药就已经在增加。

sentences.en: This is partly because of a change in general diagnostic measures in 2013.
sentences.zh: 这部分要归因于2013年一般诊断标准的变化。

sentences.en: Those changes expanded the definition of ADHD and reduced the number of signs, or symptoms, required for diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 这些变化扩大了对多动症的定义，并减少了确诊所需的体征或症状数量。

sentences.en: But cases really seemed to increase in 2020, when schools closed and many adults were forced to work from home.
sentences.zh: 但病例似乎真的在2020年增加了，当时学校关闭，许多成年人被迫在家工作。

sentences.en: “It’s very difficult to focus when you are home and you have kids,” Claussen said.
sentences.zh: “在家里有孩子的时候，很难集中注意力，”克劳森说。

sentences.en: She said such conditions may have worsened ADHD symptoms in people with less severe cases.
sentences.zh: 她说，这种情况可能会加重轻度患者的ADHD症状。

sentences.en: Experts say that it was long believed that ADHD was underdiagnosed in adults.
sentences.zh: 专家表示，长期以来人们一直认为成人ADHD被漏诊。

sentences.en: Now, experts debate about whether it has become over-diagnosed.
sentences.zh: 如今，专家就其是否已被过度诊断展开争论。

sentences.en: There is no blood or brain test for the disorder.
sentences.zh: 这种疾病没有血液或脑部检测。

sentences.en: Experts say it is diagnosed when symptoms cause ongoing problems in more than one area of life, and when those symptoms began in early childhood.
sentences.zh: 专家表示，当症状在生活的多个领域持续造成困扰，且这些症状始于童年早期时，即可作出诊断。

sentences.en: Experts say the best way professionals diagnose ADHD is by getting careful histories from patients and from people who know them.
sentences.zh: 专家表示，专业人士诊断ADHD的最佳方式是详细了解患者的病史，并了解其周围人的情况。

sentences.en: They also might test a patient’s memory and ability to focus.
sentences.zh: 他们还可能测试患者的记忆力和注意力。

sentences.en: But getting an appointment with a mental health professional can take months.
sentences.zh: 然而，预约精神健康专业人士可能要等上几个月。

sentences.en: And assessments can cost thousands of dollars.
sentences.zh: 而且评估费用可能高达数千美元。

sentences.en: Many people turn to family doctors.
sentences.zh: 许多人转而求助于家庭医生。

sentences.en: People also take online diagnostic tests, some of which are linked to health companies that prescribe medications.
sentences.zh: 人们还会进行在线诊断测试，其中一些与开具处方的健康公司挂钩。

sentences.en: “There is a wide variability in this country in how people diagnose, how strict they are, and who they diagnose,” said Margaret Sibley.
sentences.zh: “在这个国家，人们在诊断方式、严格程度以及诊断对象上都存在很大差异，”玛格丽特·西布利说。

sentences.en: She is psychologist at University of Washington.
sentences.zh: 她是华盛顿大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: The American Professional Society of ADHD and Related Disorders is preparing a set of diagnosis and treatment guidelines for American health professionals who treat adults.
sentences.zh: 美国ADHD及相关 disorder 专业协会正在为治疗成人的美国医疗专业人员制定一套诊断和治疗指南。

sentences.en: Sibley is leading the work on the guidelines, which the organization expects to release later this year.
sentences.zh: 西布利正在牵头制定这些指南，该组织预计将于今年晚些时候发布。

sentences.en: And I'm Jill Robbins.
sentences.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

glossary.zh: 青少年 (n.): 13至19岁的少年；十几岁的孩子

glossary.zh: 诊断 (v.): 识别疾病；判断病情

glossary.zh: 诊所 (n.): 提供医疗救治而不留夜的医疗机构

glossary.zh: 评估 (n.): 对事物做出判断；评定

glossary.zh: 心理学家 (n.): 研究心理与行为；治疗精神疾病者

glossary.zh: 处方 (v.): 开药方；指示使用
